project.name: Your project name
project.type: e.g. Next.js SaaS app, Rust CLI, Python data pipeline
project.purpose: One sentence: what this codebase does and who uses it.

stack.tests: How changes are verified here — test runner, CI, or manual steps.

codebase_map.responsibility: One line: what this file owns.
codebase_map.known_issue: Optional: a known bug, debt, or migration target.

engineering_standards: Keep behavior-compatible public interfaces unless a breaking change is explicitly approved.
Prefer small, reviewable commits with tests around changed behavior.
Do not mix broad mechanical migrations with semantic behavior changes without an approved rollout plan.
Name the verification you would run; never claim a verification passed unless it actually ran.
direct_work_examples: Localized bug fix with a clear root cause and obvious verification.
Adding a missing guard or error path inside one module.
Refactoring one file without changing its public contract.
Writing focused tests for known behavior.
advisor_work_examples: Changing a public API used by multiple modules.
Choosing between compatibility wrappers, full rewrites, or staged migrations.
Combining a behavior change with a broad mechanical refactor.
Security-sensitive auth/session behavior or anything that moves money.
Any migration where rollback, compatibility, or test strategy is unclear.
